text: Fill in the correct term for each principle of skin incisions.
questions: The cleavage lines found by puncturing cadaver skin are called *Langer's/Langer:Named after the anatomist who first described them.* lines.
An incision *parallel:Should the incision run along or across the lines?* to these lines heals with a fine scar because it runs between collagen bundles.
An incision across the lines produces a wider scar because *tension:What force acts on the wound edges when collagen bundles are cut?* pulls the wound edges apart.
A straight incision crossing a joint flexion crease risks forming a *contracture:What happens when scar tissue shortens across a joint?* that limits movement.

overallFeedback.feedback: Langer's lines map the dominant collagen orientation in each region of the skin. An incision parallel to them separates rather than cuts collagen bundles, producing less wound tension and a finer scar; an incision perpendicular to them is pulled apart and widens. At flexion creases a longitudinal scar contracts and restricts joint movement (contracture), so surgeons zigzag or curve the incision.
